guides.definition: Creates a numeric array and calculates its mean and standard deviation. Requires NumPy in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Numeric sequence used to create the array.

examples.title: Summarize measurements
examples.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([10, 12, 9, 11], dtype=float)
mean = values.mean()
standard_deviation = values.std()
examples.explanation: NumPy performs vectorized numeric reductions; choose ddof=1 for the conventional sample standard deviation.

guides.definition: Builds a boolean mask and selects matching NumPy array values. Requires NumPy in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install it.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Sequence used to create the array.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Value compared with every array element.

examples.title: Select values at least ten
examples.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([4, 10, 12, 3])
selected = values[values >= 10]
examples.explanation: The comparison produces one boolean per element; indexing with that mask returns only matching values.

guides.definition: Uses NumPy linear algebra to solve Ax = b. Requires NumPy in the selected Python environment; Hypershell does not install it.

examples.title: Solve two equations
examples.code:
import numpy as np

matrix = np.array([[3, 1], [1, 2]], dtype=float)
vector = np.array([9, 8], dtype=float)
solution = np.linalg.solve(matrix, vector)
examples.explanation: solve requires a square, non-singular coefficient matrix and returns the vector satisfying the system within floating-point precision.
